fare.note: Multiple Stopover Service. ANA defines a stopover as a stay at a transfer point of MORE THAN 24 HOURS. Two stopovers per direction, the first free and the second subject to fees plus consumption tax. Emphasis is on adding Japanese DOMESTIC destinations (50+ airports), so it fits 'Seattle to Seoul with two nights in Tokyo' far better than a single overnight, and fits 'Seattle to Tokyo plus Osaka' best of all.
Mirrors ANA's structure closely. The 24-hour stopover definition is an industry norm and is assumed to apply, but was NOT verified against JAL's own pages - lower confidence than the ANA row.

hotel.note: Requires an email request at least one day before travel to confirm eligibility - not automatic.
Directly relevant to a US origin. Verify the itinerary qualifies.

fare.note: Some sources cite stopovers permitted up to 90 days under fare rules; 7 days is the commonly quoted free window from North America.

fee.note: applies to some booking classes only

fare.note: No advertised stopover programme. However, multi-city pricing on EVA's own site is frequently at or below the equivalent connecting fare, so the stopover is effectively free in practice. Worth surfacing precisely because no listicle covers it - but state clearly that there is no published programme behind it.
Supported via multi-city booking; the branded product is a paid package rather than a free fare stopover.

hotel.note: Programme relaunched 2025; includes hotel nights for premium cabins plus Changi shopping vouchers.
One of the most generous published thresholds. Verify point-of-sale conditions.

IMPORTANT: applies only where no shorter connection is available. A deliberately chosen long layover will normally DISQUALIFY the passenger. This is the clearest documented example of the trap described in the README.
Free transit accommodation for shorter qualifying layovers. A SEPARATE programme from the paid Stopover below, with different rules - the two are routinely confused.
Free nights in a 3-star hotel via voucher issued after booking. NOT guaranteed, and the passenger must make the reservation themselves - present as conditional, never as included.

fare.note: The archetypal stopover programme. No hotel included, but the booking engine supports stopover routing directly - unusually, no multi-city workaround needed. Up to 21 days on Saga Premium Flex.
Portugal Stopover. No increase in ticket price. Bookable at purchase or added later via Manage Booking. Partner discounts on hotels and experiences rather than a free hotel.
Book via the multi-city function on Finnair's own site. Commonly cited for summer Europe itineraries; confirm year-round applicability.
Panama Stopover. Details unconfirmed - free-day allowance and fees need verification against Copa's own pages.
